subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI Codex OAuth migration leaves stale default profile and codexPlugins app inventory can fail Codex harness

question: When a usable account-scoped OpenAI OAuth profile exists but stale managed profiles or order references remain, should doctor automatically migrate and remove them after complete identity and reference proof, or preserve them behind an explicit profile-management workflow?
rationale: Credential removal is upgrade-sensitive and agent-scoped; the defect is established, but the permanent cleanup and ownership policy cannot be inferred safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Lossless doctor migration
options.body: Build a per-agent plan that proves identity, retargets config, auth order, last-good state, cron payloads, and model-map references, then removes only fully unreferenced stale profiles.

options.title: Explicit profile management
options.body: Keep doctor warning-only and add safe list, remove, or disable commands with reference diagnostics so operators control credential deletion.

options.title: Warn and preserve
options.body: Continue skipping unusable profiles at runtime while retaining stale records indefinitely and accepting ongoing health and status noise.

recommendation.title: Lossless doctor migration
recommendation.body: Build a per-agent plan that proves identity, retargets config, auth order, last-good state, cron payloads, and model-map references, then removes only fully unreferenced stale profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: They led the current Codex/OpenAI identity fold and documented the safety requirements that deferred this cleanup.
